speaker: Kimi K3
text: HDFC Bank's 5-year CAGR of -1.3% and a 30% drop from its high tell you the compounding engine has stalled, even with a 3.8% dividend yield. The 10x goal needs 21% annually for a decade; this bank has delivered 9% over ten years, so it's a wealth preserver, not a multiplier. On your IPO question: US IPOs usually require a $2,500+ account minimum and allocation is pro-rata, so $10 gets you zero shares; Indian IPOs need a demat account and UPI block of ₹10k-₹15k per lot, so ₹10k budget fits one lot but allotment is a lottery. For Reliance on Zerodha delivery: zero brokerage, but STT ₹20, exchange ₹0.59, SEBI ₹0.02, stamp ₹1.50, GST ₹0.11, DP ₹15.93 — total ₹38.15 round-trip (0.38%), plus 20% short-term tax if sold within a year.

text: The VIX jumping 13% while the S&P drops 1.8% is the market pricing in a wider range of outcomes — exactly the environment where a 10x target forces you into lottery tickets that usually expire worthless.
